clue.text: From beginning to end

parts.note: read as the whole span of something, here the stretch running from a person's birth to their death

explanation.definitionFit: The whole duration of a life runs from its beginning at birth to its end at death.

clue.text: Copper taken in by wandering six-footer

indicators.note: taken in by means enclosed, so the metal goes inside the other word

parts.note: someone wandering has lost their way
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman is fooled by a tall drifter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element's symbol; 'six-footer' is not a tall man but an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so a locust is a creature with six feet.

clue.text: He just won't eat more quickly

explanation.definitionFit: One who goes without food is a faster, and faster is also the comparative of fast, meaning speedier.

clue.text: A large number entering the examination are most dull

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so these letters sit within the exam

parts.note: an examination is a test
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Many candidates sitting the paper are very boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame means unexciting or dull, so the superlative is the dullest.

clue.text: 1 across orders a postman about right and left

indicators.note: orders means arranges, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to a mail carrier about turning right and left.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across' points to that clue's answer, which this phrase also defines. 'about' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's mortal span is the length of their life on earth.

clue.text: The principal can make a good man turn pale

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is the crossword's usual good man

indicators.note: to turn here is to change shape, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A headteacher can make a decent fellow go white with fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' signals the anagram; ST is the crossword's standard abbreviation for a saint, the 'good man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is the chief or principal item, as in the staple food of a region.

clue.text: Article on cat and bird-could be killing!

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' places one piece after another, so the article follows the cat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
A is the indefinite article
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A piece written about a cat and a bird of prey that might end in death.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used as a weapon, so it might well kill.

clue.text: She has to cut everything back

parts.note: to prune is to cut back

indicators.note: back means returned, so the word for everything is read in reverse

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A woman has to trim everything back in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal. 'She' looks like a pronoun but defines a girl's name; prune is also the plum fruit, so the name hides a garden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is a woman's given name, so a she.

clue.text: Calls in faulty equipment. It lessens the danger

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found inside the following words, running across them

parts.words: faulty equipment. It lessens the danger

explanation.surface: Safety notice: faulty kit, reduced risk.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'equipmENT. IT LESsens'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle a book or person is to name them, which is to call them.

clue.text: Change just material

parts.note: small change is loose cash
just, as in 'only', means mere

explanation.surface: Swapping nothing but a piece of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool fabric made from goat hair.

clue.text: A horse giving full value

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A racehorse that repays its whole price.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount of something is its total sum or value.

clue.text: His stock is very small, but should grow

definitions.text: His stock is very small, but should grow

parts.words: His stock is very small, but should grow
parts.note: the stock is a trader's goods, tiny items that are meant to sprout and grow

explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in seeds keeps a stock of tiny grains that will grow into plants.

clue.text: The rat may well constitute a menace

indicators.note: may well suggests the letters could equally be arranged in another way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A rodent is likely to be a danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The rodent sits in the surface as itself, but its six letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is something that menaces or endangers.

clue.text: Masculine beast, not heartless but spiteful

parts.note: masculine means male
a vole is a small animal

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle, so the middle letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A male animal, not cruel but vindictive.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent means wishing harm on others, so spiteful.

clue.text: There's greater than usual concern about savage writer

parts.note: OS, outsize, is a size greater than usual

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: concern, as in worry or attention, means care
savage means wild

explanation.surface: Unusual worry about a fierce author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. OS (outsize) is a clothing label for sizes larger than usual; the writer is the Irish author of The Picture of Dorian Gray.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright and wit who wrote The Importance of Being Earnest is a famous author.

clue.text: Puts up with relatives-is on guard

parts.note: to put up with is to bear
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Tolerates the family while standing on sentry duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall fur cap worn by guardsmen on sentry duty outside Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: A plant requires proper drainage

indicators.note: proper suggests the letters are put right, arranged correctly into another word

explanation.surface: A garden shrub needs good soil drainage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardenia is a fragrant flowering shrub.

clue.text: Cry for mercy when putting one's queen in the pool

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the pool

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pool
one's read as I'S, I is
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A plea for pity on throwing a chess queen into a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserere is the psalm beginning 'have mercy', and hence any plea for mercy.

clue.text: Got out-given aid-reacted badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone was rescued with help and then responded poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to root out or remove completely, so got out in the sense of removed.

clue.text: Run personal transport always

parts.note: a car is personal transport
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Drive one's own vehicle at all times.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along headlong, so to run.

clue.text: Face presented by the wise $ man after six

indicators.note: after places the wise man's word behind the numeral

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A countenance shown by the wise man after six.
explanation.definitionFit: A visage is a person's face.

clue.text: Resent having to change notes

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Resent having to alter the notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter something is to note it down in a record.

clue.text: Some soldiers think it's to liberate

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
to deem is to think or judge

explanation.surface: Some troops believe it is right to free people.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem someone is to free them, for example by paying a ransom.

clue.text: The same people are present

parts.note: DO, short for ditto, means the same again
a people is a nation

explanation.surface: Those identical folk are all here.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, and a present is also a gift.

clue.text: German children appear more considerate

explanation.surface: Young people in Germany seem better mannered.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinder is German for children, and in English it is the comparative of kind, meaning more thoughtful.

clue.text: Sing, unperturbed about puff needed

indicators.note: about means going round, so the calm word wraps around the other

parts.note: unperturbed means calm or serene
a puff is a promotional plug, an ad

explanation.surface: Sing, calm despite being short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To serenade is to sing to someone, traditionally beneath a window.

clue.text: Dined in quarters, being tidy

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the meal word goes inside the compass points

parts.note: the quarters are compass points: north, east and north again
dined means ate

explanation.surface: Having eaten in their lodgings, the soldiers are made orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass quarters N, E, N take ATE between E and the final N.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten something is to make it orderly.

clue.text: Quite dark lead-inferior

parts.note: the lead in a film is its star
inferior means lesser, less

explanation.surface: A gloomy, second-rate leading part.
explanation.definitionFit: A night sky with no stars showing is completely dark.
